summary.what: guest boot time at the shell prompt
microVM boot (`virt` kernel, whole OS in RAM)
summary.conditions: QEMU `microvm`, release `kwickos-amd64.efi` and initramfs, median of 10 (guest 0.19-0.69 s, wall 0.40-1.15 s)

summary.what: memory in use after boot (live ISO)
summary.conditions: `MemTotal - MemAvailable` at the prompt, range of 10 runs (medians 66.3 and 49.6). Alpine keeps its root file system in RAM: 11 MiB of its 15 MiB shmem (the other 4 MiB is the QEMU display's framebuffer, which KwickOS has too). Without the RAM root Alpine is about 55 MiB, so KwickOS still uses about 5 MiB less like for like. The live root's LZMA dictionary is 64 KiB: with main's earlier automatic dictionary the kernel held 4 MiB of decompression buffers per CPU and KwickOS measured 53-59 MiB here (2026-11-23-vm-3-before.txt)
unique package names in Alpine main + community and in Debian trixie, trixie-updates and trixie-security main, the sources KwickOS's apt uses

`du -skx /` / 1024 after installing, package indexes and caches removed, fresh container each. KwickOS: the 0.7.0 image with main's kpkg (0.81 MB smaller) and `lean-builds = true`, so `apt install PKG` installs the KwickOS lean musl build (`kwick-PKG`, built from upstream source by scripts/build-musl-lean.sh, not yet in a release). In parentheses: Debian's packages on KwickOS (`apt install --no-lean`) and Debian slim (2026-11-23-container-2.txt). curl 8.23.0 with mbedTLS 4.1.2, nghttp2 and zlib, static, plus the Mozilla CA bundle; Alpine's curl 8.23.0 also has IDN, PSL, brotli and zstd (neither has NTLM). Alpine's 13.8 MB includes OpenSSL and the CA bundle from its base image

`du -skx /` / 1024 after installing, package indexes and caches removed, fresh container each. KwickOS: the 0.7.0 image with main's kpkg (0.81 MB smaller) and `lean-builds = true`, so `apt install PKG` installs the KwickOS lean musl build (`kwick-PKG`, built from upstream source by scripts/build-musl-lean.sh, not yet in a release). In parentheses: Debian's packages on KwickOS (`apt install --no-lean`) and Debian slim (2026-11-23-container-2.txt). CPython 3.14.10 like Alpine's, standard library as a deflated zip with source and bytecode (Alpine installs source plus python3-pyc), ssl and hashlib built in with OpenSSL 3.5.9, sqlite3, ctypes, curses, readline; pip, venv and musllinux wheels work. Left out: gdbm modules and tkinter (Alpine splits tkinter out too)

summary.what: installed size with nginx / openssh-server / git
summary.conditions: `du -skx /` / 1024 after installing, package indexes and caches removed, fresh container each. KwickOS: the 0.7.0 image with main's kpkg (0.81 MB smaller) and `lean-builds = true`, so `apt install PKG` installs the KwickOS lean musl build (`kwick-PKG`, built from upstream source by scripts/build-musl-lean.sh, not yet in a release). In parentheses: Debian's packages on KwickOS (`apt install --no-lean`) and Debian slim (2026-11-23-container-2.txt). nginx 1.30.7 static with LibreSSL 4.4.1 (HTTP/2, HTTP/3, TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768), no dynamic modules; OpenSSH 10.6p2 server and ssh-keygen with LibreSSL's libcrypto (Alpine: 10.3p1 with OpenSSL), no PAM or moduli file, as in Alpine; git 2.56.1 static (Alpine: 2.54.1) without Perl, Tcl/Tk, git-daemon or scalar, as in Alpine. nginx and openssh-server win by 0.5 and 0.2 MB, less than the 2.1 MB base image difference: the packages themselves are larger than Alpine's, whose base already carries musl and OpenSSL
